prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Reform UK’s “Contract” outlines first-100-days priorities, longer-term plans, and costings.

Core pledges
- Freeze non-essential immigration; create strict border controls.
- Stop small-boat crossings via detention, deportation, returns to France, and leaving the ECHR.
- Eliminate NHS waiting lists through staffing incentives, use of independent capacity, and patient guarantees.
- Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000; increase higher-rate threshold to £70,000.
- Cut energy bills by scrapping green levies/Net Zero and expanding domestic oil and gas.

Immigration
- Freeze non-essential visas; new Department of Immigration.
- Offshore/rapid processing; bar asylum/citizenship for arrivals from safe countries; no legal aid for non-citizens.
- Immediate deportation of foreign offenders post-sentence; potential citizenship withdrawal for serious crimes.
- Bar student dependents; restrict post-study stays to essential skills; close abuse of courses.
- Five-year residency/work for benefits; “Employer Immigration Tax” (NI 20% on foreign hires, with health/care and micro-firm exemptions).
- Estimated savings: £5–10bn p.a.; employer tax: £4bn p.a.

Public spending and regulation
- Stop paying interest on QE reserves to banks (~£35bn p.a. saving).
- 5% efficiency saving across departments (£50bn p.a.).
- Halve foreign aid (£6bn p.a.); improve HMRC tax collection; scrap retained EU rules.

Economy (personal)
- Lift income tax start point to £20,000; lower fuel duty by 20p/litre.
- Scrap VAT on energy and environmental levies (~£500/household).
- Cut stamp duty: 0% up to £750k; 2% to £1.5m; 4% above.
- Restore VAT-free tourist shopping.
- IHT: 0% under £2m; 20% above (charity option).
- Cost: £70bn p.a.

Economy (business)
- No corporation tax on profits up to £100k; main rate to 20%, then 15% (year 3).
- Abolish IR35; raise VAT threshold to £150k.
- Abolish business rates for high-street SMEs; 4% online delivery tax on large multinationals; entrepreneurs’ tax to 5%.
- Planning reform; major deregulatory and tax simplification drive.
- Cost: £18bn p.a.

NHS
- Zero basic-rate income tax for NHS/social care frontline for 3 years; end training caps; write off fees via service.
- Use independent/not-for-profit capacity; 20% tax relief on private care/insurance.
- Patient vouchers if access targets missed (GP 3 days; consultant 3 weeks; operation 9 weeks).
- Efficiency measures; charge for missed appointments; “Pharmacy First.”
- Cost: £17bn p.a.

Energy/Net Zero
- Scrap Net Zero and related subsidies; end £10bn renewables subsidies via equivalent taxes.
- Fast-track North Sea oil/gas; pilot shale; expand nuclear SMRs and other technologies.
- Savings: ~£30bn p.a.

Policing and justice
- Recruit 40,000 officers; expand stop and search; tougher sentences for violent and drug crimes.
- Increase justice budget to £12bn; build 10,000 prison places; revise hate-crime definition.
- Cost: policing £3bn p.a.; justice £2bn p.a.

Other areas (highlights)
- Education: curriculum balance; restrict gender-related policies in schools; parental notification; single-sex facilities; 20% tax relief on independent schooling; scrap student loan interest; expand PRUs; 2‑year degrees. Cost: £5bn p.a.
- Benefits: stricter work requirements (two-offer rule; four-month limit); face-to-face assessments; apprenticeships. Savings: £15bn p.a.
- Brexit: scrap retained EU law; abandon Windsor Framework; prepare wider renegotiations.
- Defence: spend to 2.5% GDP by year 3, 3% by year 6; pay rise; legal protections; veteran department; industry/procurement reform. Cost: £14bn p.a.
- Housing: faster brownfield planning; local priority for social housing; restore mortgage interest deductibility; leasehold reform. Neutral cost.
- Families: transferable marriage allowance; front-loaded child benefit (ages 1–4); single-sex spaces; tighter smartphone controls. Cost: £8bn p.a.
- Transport/infrastructure: scrap HS2 (save £25bn one-off); end ULEZ/CAZ/LTNs; regional upgrades; restructure utilities (50% public/50% UK pensions), cap standing charges. Savings: £5bn p.a.
- Agriculture/fishing: increase farm budget to £3bn; revise subsidies; curb foreign fishing access; expand patrols; rebuild processing. Cost: £4bn p.a.
- Pensions/social care: Royal Commission; curb offshore tax practices in care; system reforms.
- Constitutional and governance: leave ECHR; reform Human Rights Act, Lords, civil service, postal voting; PR referendum; Bill of Rights; BBC licence fee abolition; free speech bill; anti-corruption unit.

Funding summary
- Claimed annual savings: ~£150bn; extra growth tax take: £10bn; total £160bn p.a. versus total costs £141bn p.a. over a five-year term.
